eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 13 · Aggregation and Aging

code:
SELECT invoice_num,
  CASE
    WHEN TRUNC(SYSDATE) - due_date <= 0 THEN 'Current'
    WHEN TRUNC(SYSDATE) - due_date BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN '1-30 Days'
    WHEN TRUNC(SYSDATE) - due_date BETWEEN 31 AND 60 THEN '31-60 Days'
    WHEN TRUNC(SYSDATE) - due_date BETWEEN 61 AND 90 THEN '61-90 Days'
    ELSE '90+ Days'
  END AS aging_bucket
FROM ap_payment_schedules_all;
caption: CASE returns the result of the first matching WHEN, top to bottom.

steps.label: NO OVERLAP
steps.sub: each day falls in exactly one bucket

steps.label: NO GAPS
steps.sub: ELSE catches everything past the last bucket

code:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN TRUNC(SYSDATE)-due_date<=0 THEN 'Current' ... END AS aging_bucket,
  SUM(amount_remaining) AS total_outstanding
FROM ap_payment_schedules_all
WHERE amount_remaining > 0
GROUP BY
  CASE WHEN TRUNC(SYSDATE)-due_date<=0 THEN 'Current' ... END;
caption: GROUP BY repeats the full CASE expression — Oracle groups by what it evaluates to.
